nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that distinguishes genuine utterance ambiguity from model uncertainty under unseen compositional structures.
requirements: Achieve ambiguity-detection F1 ≥0.85 on unseen compositions, using independently annotated sets of valid interpretations.
Match unambiguous-input execution accuracy of a single-output parser trained on identical data.

nodes.content: Train a shared encoder with execution and interpretation-set heads on annotated parse sets; detect ambiguity from predicted cardinality, not entropy.
Can supervised interpretation-set cardinality distinguish genuine alternative parses from high-entropy errors on unseen compositions?
On unseen COGS-AMB compositions, cardinality supervision yields ambiguity F1 ≥0.85, exceeding entropy-thresholding by ≥0.10 without reducing unambiguous execution accuracy.
Independently annotate COGS-AMB sets; train matched-data cardinality and single-output parsers; compare cardinality-versus-entropy F1 and unambiguous execution accuracy on novel compositions.
Run five-seed COGS-AMB novel-composition splits; compare cardinality, entropy, and matched-data single-output baselines on ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution accuracy.
Across five COGS-AMB seeds, cardinality achieved F1 0.87 versus entropy 0.74; unambiguous execution accuracy matched single-output at 91%.
Adopt cardinality-based ambiguity detection: COGS-AMB F1 exceeds 0.85, and unambiguous execution matches the single-output baseline.
Integrate the adopted cardinality detector into parser serving, returning ranked interpretation sets only for predicted ambiguous utterances.
Parser API v0.1 returns ranked interpretation sets for predicted ambiguities and one executable parse otherwise, with cardinality scores.
Across label-preserving paraphrases matched on entropy, multi-interpretation predictions persist for ≥80% ambiguous inputs versus ≤20% uncertain unambiguous inputs.
Using Parser API v0.1, test three independently validated interpretation-set-preserving paraphrases per 400 entropy-matched COGS-AMB examples for multi-interpretation persistence.
On 400 entropy-matched examples, multi-interpretation predictions persisted across paraphrases for only 62% of ambiguous inputs versus 17% unambiguous inputs.
Augment cardinality training with interpretation-set-preserving paraphrases, then re-evaluate unseen-composition ambiguity F1, paraphrase stability, and matched-data unambiguous execution accuracy.
Use Parser API v0.1 to select unstable, set-preserving COGS-AMB paraphrases; fine-tune cardinality consistency and repeat five-seed evaluation.
Parser API v0.2 includes paraphrase-consistent cardinality weights and a five-seed COGS-AMB report of F1, stability, and execution accuracy.
Audit Parser API v0.2 on independently annotated COGS-AMB compositions versus v0.1 and single-output baselines for F1, paraphrase stability, execution accuracy.
On independently annotated COGS-AMB, v0.2 achieved ambiguity F1 0.88, paraphrase stability 83% versus 62%, and unambiguous execution 91%, matching single-output.
Use grammar-constrained candidate decoding and conformal abstention; flag ambiguity only when multiple semantically distinct interpretations have annotation-calibrated support.
Can conformal support distinguish valid alternative interpretations from beam-search artifacts on unseen compositions without degrading unambiguous execution accuracy?
Using Parser API v0.2, compare grammar-constrained conformal and cardinality detection on unseen COGS-AMB for F1, beam-artifact rejection, execution accuracy.
On independently annotated COGS-AMB recursive-composition holdouts, cardinality ambiguity F1 was 0.79 versus conformal 0.86, below the required 0.85.
Conformal support maintains ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 on recursive compositions while matching the 91% unambiguous execution baseline.
Annotate recursive COGS-AMB beam artifacts; calibrate conformal support on disjoint data; compare artifact rejection, F1, and 91% execution baseline.
Against Parser API v0.2, calibrate conformal support on disjoint COGS-AMB data; measure recursive-holdout F1, artifact rejection, execution accuracy.
On recursive COGS-AMB holdouts, conformal support achieved ambiguity F1 0.86 and 89% artifact rejection, but execution 88% versus 91% baseline.
Restricting conformal support to ambiguity classification while preserving v0.2's execution path yields recursive-holdout F1 ≥0.85 and execution ≥91%.
Attach a conformal ambiguity gate to Parser API v0.2 without changing execution decoding; test recursive COGS-AMB F1 and execution accuracy.
Gate-only conformal support scored recursive-holdout ambiguity F1 0.82, below 0.85, despite preserving 91% unambiguous execution accuracy.
Restoring grammar-constrained candidate decoding for the conformal gate while retaining v0.2's execution output yields recursive F1 ≥0.85 and accuracy ≥91%.
Add grammar-constrained candidates to v0.2's conformal gate, retain its execution decoder, and measure recursive-holdout F1 and accuracy.
On recursive COGS-AMB holdouts, grammar-constrained conformal gating reached ambiguity F1 0.86; unchanged v0.2 decoding retained 91% unambiguous execution accuracy.
Adopt grammar-constrained conformal gating with unchanged v0.2 execution decoding: recursive-holdout F1 reaches 0.86 and execution remains 91%.
Implement the adopted grammar-constrained conformal gate in Parser API v0.2, retaining its execution decoder and logging supported interpretation sets.
Parser API v0.3 replaces v0.2's cardinality ambiguity gate with grammar-constrained conformal gating, retaining execution decoding and logging supported interpretation sets.
Can semantic-equivalence filtering prevent grammar-constrained beams from counting equivalent logical forms as ambiguity on unseen compositions?
Test v0.3 beam clustering by alpha-renaming and conjunction reordering on 300 annotated unseen compositions; measure false-ambiguity reduction.
On 300 annotated unseen compositions, equivalence clustering removed 27 of 34 false-ambiguity flags without merging any validated interpretation pairs.
Integrate validated equivalence clustering before conformal scoring, recalibrate support, and retest COGS-AMB ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution accuracy.
Add validated alpha-renaming and conjunction-order clustering to v0.3 beams; recalibrate conformal scores on disjoint COGS-AMB data.
Parser API v0.4 adds equivalence-clustered beams and recalibrated conformal support to v0.3, leaving its execution decoder unchanged.
Compare v0.4 against v0.3 on independently annotated COGS-AMB holdouts for duplicate-parse false alarms, ambiguity F1, and unambiguous execution accuracy.
On 300 annotated COGS-AMB holdouts, v0.4 cut duplicate-parse false alarms 34→7, raised ambiguity F1 0.86→0.89, retained 91% unambiguous execution.
Select v0.4's equivalence-clustered conformal parser: ambiguity F1 reaches 0.89, duplicate false alarms fall, and unambiguous execution remains 91%.
Train a contrastive interpretation verifier on compositional minimal pairs to reject unsupported readings while retaining v0.4's execution decoder.
Does contrastive verification reject structurally plausible but invalid readings on deeper unseen compositions without removing valid ambiguous interpretations?
On depth-4 COGS-AMB, contrastive verification rejects ≥70% invalid readings, retains ≥95% valid readings, and preserves 91% execution accuracy.
Train a minimal-pair verifier on v0.4 candidates; measure invalid-reading rejection, valid-reading retention, and execution accuracy on annotated depth-4 COGS-AMB.
On annotated depth-4 COGS-AMB, verification rejected 74% invalid readings but retained only 89% valid readings; execution remained 91%.
Hard-positive augmentation raises depth-4 valid-reading retention from 89% to ≥95%, preserving ≥70% invalid-reading rejection and 91% execution accuracy.
Augment v0.4 candidate-verifier training with validated depth-3 hard positives; retest depth-4 retention, rejection, ambiguity F1, and execution.
On depth-4 COGS-AMB, hard positives raised valid-reading retention 89%→96%; invalid-reading rejection reached 71%, ambiguity F1 0.87, execution 91%.
Adopt hard-positive verification: depth-4 valid-reading retention rises 89%→96%, invalid-reading rejection reaches 71%, ambiguity F1 0.87, execution 91%.
Train five bootstrap parsers; flag ambiguity when two distinct readings each recur in ≥4 models, retaining v0.4's execution decoder.
Does cross-bootstrap recurrence reflect genuine interpretation multiplicity rather than shared compositional errors on unseen structures?
Train five matched-data bootstrap parsers; compare recurrence gating against v0.4 on independently annotated depth-4 COGS-AMB ambiguity F1 and error overlap.
Score five bootstrap parsers on 500 annotated depth-4 COGS-AMB utterances; inspect recurrent candidate sets and compare recurrence versus v0.4 F1.
Depth-4 recurrence audit lists each utterance's five bootstrap candidate sets, annotated valid readings, shared-error labels, and F1 comparisons against v0.4.
Quantify shared-error false alarms in the depth-4 recurrence audit; compare ≥4-of-5 gating against v0.4 on ambiguity F1.
Among 500 depth-4 utterances, recurrence F1 was 0.79 versus v0.4's 0.86; shared errors caused 31 false alarms.
Would template-stratified bootstraps reduce the 31 shared-error false alarms without losing valid alternative readings?
Template-stratified bootstraps cut shared-error false alarms from 31 to ≤15 while raising depth-4 ambiguity F1 from 0.79 to ≥0.85.
Use the 31-error audit to stratify bootstrap training by compositional template; retest shared-error alarms, ambiguity F1, and valid-reading retention.
Train five template-stratified bootstraps; benchmark ≥4-of-5 gating against v0.4 on audited depth-4 false alarms, ambiguity F1, and valid-reading retention.
On 500 depth-4 utterances, stratified recurrence cut shared-error alarms 31→12 and raised ambiguity F1 0.79→0.86; valid-reading retention was 95%.
Keep v0.4 in production: stratified five-parser recurrence matches its 0.86 depth-4 F1, while unstratified gating scored 0.79.
